summary: Phase 3 of suite deployment mode: a new fire-and-forget event bus (infra/eventbus, in-process by default, Redis when clustered) fans node events and notifications out to every myseliasan instance, closing the last documented Phase 1 gap -- a fleet rule whose clauses span nodes attached to DIFFERENT instances used to never arm at all (it went quiet rather than firing twice) -- and, as a side effect of the same wiring, makes the live notification feed (SSE) span the deployment too, so a browser connected to any instance now sees everything the deployment raises rather than only what its own instance ingested. apps/myseliasan/services/node_events.go defines two topics deliberately: 'node-events' carries the RAW node event so every instance's correlator sees what the origin's did (never the control plane's own re-published notification, which would let one rule's alert satisfy another rule's clause), and 'notifications' relays EVERY notification an instance publishes -- a node's, but equally a node-lost alert, a certificate-expiry warning, or the daily digest -- to the other instances' live feeds via a new domain/notification.Service.RelayToStream (stream-only, never re-persisted, since the origin already wrote the row). infra/config.ClusterConfigModel gains eventBusProvider, which DEFAULTS TO cache.provider rather than needing its own setting, since a deployment that already pointed the cache at Redis has already answered whether instances have somewhere shared to meet; eventbus.New returns an error on an unrecognised provider rather than silently degrading to in-process, since that would leave a clustered deployment looking configured while delivering to nobody. Live-verified on two Postgres+Redis instances with a real adopted node: killing the node on instance A (which never held its control channel) delivered the 'Node offline' alert on instance B's live SSE feed, carrying the origin's own notification id. Benching this phase also found and fixed two PRE-EXISTING bugs unrelated to clustering itself: (1) the live notification feed died 30 seconds after opening on every install, standalone included, because Go's http.Server.WriteTimeout is an absolute deadline that never resets as more is written -- fixed by extending the response's write deadline (http.NewResponseController) before every write and on a 20s heartbeat, so the stream lives as long as it is being consumed rather than never expiring at all, plus adding the missing Unwrap() method to the request-log middleware's ResponseWriter wrapper, without which ResponseController could not reach the real connection at all and the deadline fix silently did nothing; (2) the fleet's own parent certificate (its cert and private key stored in two separate un-locked rows) could be permanently corrupted when two instances issued at the same moment and their writes interleaved, leaving one instance's certificate beside the other's key -- undetected at write time and persisting forever, since every later boot found both rows non-empty and handed them straight to the mTLS listener, which then refused to start and left every adopted node dark until an operator cleared the rows by hand. Fixed by validating the stored pair (tls.X509KeyPair) on every read and re-issuing on mismatch, and by writing the key before the certificate so a concurrent reader sees either the old matching pair or a key with no certificate yet, never a certificate that looks current beside a key that does not belong to it.
compatibility: The SSE write-deadline fix affects EVERY myseliasan install, including standalone, retroactively: before this change, the live notification feed silently dropped anything published during the 30-second-cycle reconnect gap on every deployment that has ever kept the /api/notifications/stream connection open, with nothing logged -- there is no configuration flag or migration involved, the fix simply applies on upgrade. The fleet-certificate fix SELF-HEALS an install already broken by the pre-existing bug: the next read of the parent certificate after upgrading detects a mismatched stored pair and re-issues a valid one automatically, with no manual database edit required (a control plane whose fleet mTLS listener was already failing to start with "private key does not match public key" starts working again on the next call, no operator action needed). The event bus itself introduces no required configuration: cluster.eventBusProvider defaults to the existing cache.provider, so a standalone install (default in-process bus) is unaffected, and an existing Phase 1/2 clustered install that already shares a Redis cache gets fleet-rule correlation and the cross-instance live feed automatically on upgrade with no new settings to set. Setting cluster.eventBusProvider to an unrecognised value is a new hard boot-failure (previously not possible, since the field did not exist); every existing config.json has it unset.
